segments.t: Near the ASK agency, Camille Valentini and her boyfriend Samy share a romantic breakthrough. After agreeing to unite their lives, Camille tells him to dash over to the casting audition. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.

Tu es vraiment sûr de toi?
Oui, Camille et Valentini, tous les deux.
Je suis tout à fait d'accord.
Je t'aime, je veux t'épouser.
Ça tombe très bien entre nous.
On a déjà le même prénom.
Notre vie va changer complètement.
La tienne aussi va changer.
Maintenant, tu dois foncer au casting.
Qu'est-ce que tu dis?
Vas-y vite pour rattraper le coup.
Je t'aime de tout mon cœur.
Moi aussi, je t'aime beaucoup.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.

'We are going to do it together.' Camille announces their joint decision. French forms the near future by pairing the present tense of 'to go' directly with 'do'.

'Are you really sure about it?' Camille Valentini asks for certainty. The informal 'you' form around 'this line' marks a direct, personal relationship.
Oui, Camille et Valentini, tous les deux.
'Yes, Camille and Valentini, both of us.' Camille emphasizes their union. The adverb meaning 'yes' gives the reply its conversational emphasis.
Je suis tout à fait d'accord.
'I completely agree.' Camille Valentini gives wholehearted assent. The adverb meaning 'completely' gives the reply its conversational emphasis.
Je t'aime, je veux t'épouser.
'I love you, I want to marry you.' Camille declares his love and intention to marry. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'love'.
Ça tombe très bien entre nous.
'That works out very well for us.' Camille Valentini notes the happy coincidence. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'falls'.
On a déjà le même prénom.
'We already share the same first name.' Camille Valentini jokes about their identical names. Notice how 'have' leads directly into the noun meaning 'first name'.
Notre vie va changer complètement.
'Our life is going to change completely.' Camille foresees exciting transformations ahead. French forms the near future by pairing the present tense of 'to go' directly with 'change'.
La tienne aussi va changer.
'Yours will change too.' Camille Valentini replies in kind. French forms the near future by pairing the present tense of 'to go' directly with 'change'.
Maintenant, tu dois foncer au casting.
'Now, you must hurry to the casting.' Camille Valentini directs him to take action. Notice how 'must' leads directly into the noun meaning 'casting'.
Qu'est-ce que tu dis?
'What are you saying?' Camille is taken aback by the sudden shift. Notice how the short vowel drops before a vowel sound around 'say', making the phrase flow smoothly as one unit.
Vas-y vite pour rattraper le coup.
'Go there quickly to fix things.' Camille Valentini urges him to save the day. The verb meaning 'go there' pairs naturally with the noun for 'situation' in everyday conversation.
Je t'aime de tout mon cœur.
'I love you with all my heart.' Camille reaffirms his love before leaving. The verb meaning 'love' pairs naturally with the noun for 'heart' in everyday conversation.
Moi aussi, je t'aime beaucoup.
